_doc: Wind and the dangers of the coast at sea (world/seaWinds.js, systems/seaPassage.js). Off in hand-made worlds with no generationParams unless world.seaWinds is true.

winds._doc: The prevailing winds by latitude, as Terrain._climate12 has them for the rain: trades blowing west and toward the equator (|latitude| under trades.to), westerlies blowing east and poleward (to westerlies.to), polar easterlies past that; a calm doldrums belt at the equator and slack horse latitudes where the trades meet the westerlies (edgeFade). angleN / angleS: the way the wind blows TOWARD in degrees (0 east, 90 north, 180 west) in the northern / southern half. The bands follow the sun north in the northern summer by seasonShift (|latitude| units, the year's 120 days: the sun furthest north on day 45). Trades and westerlies blow harder in their hemisphere's winter by winterBoost. Day by day the wind veers up to `wander` degrees and its strength from strengthLo to strengthHi of the band's, smooth over `scale` hexes and `days` days.

sailing._doc: Point of sail: a ship's speed times this by the angle between her heading and the way the wind blows (0 running before it, 90 a beam reach, 180 dead into it — tacking), by rig. In light airs every point drifts toward `calm` (fully felt from `fullAt` strength up). An oared ship rows `oars` of her way whatever the wind. In a fjord the wind between the walls is fickle: `fjordWind` whatever the heading. rigs: by ship type (default `defaultRig`); draft scales the coast's dangers (a rowboat floats over what tears a galleon).

storms._doc: Storms that cross the sea over days. Born on the open sea (ocean / deep ocean) in their belts and seasons — hurricanes in the trade-wind belt in late summer, gales in the westerlies in winter — from a hash of the world seed and the day (no RNG drawn: the same world has the same storms, and a captain can read them coming). `slots` chances a day per `perArea` hexes of map; each carried by the prevailing wind `speed` hexes a day (hurricanes turning poleward as they age: recurve), `radius` hexes across their worst, growing and dying over `life` days, weakening by landDecay a day over land. danger = intensity, falling off to the edge; ships inside are caught as in a storm (Ships._stormAtSea).

coast._doc: The dangers of the new coast to a ship under way (systems/seaPassage.js). Per hex sailed through: risk (daylight, cautious) × atSpeed (the leg made at better than speedAt of the ship's speed, or under 'press on' orders) × night (sailed in the dark, no lighthouse in reach: lit) × draft; a pilot whose waters it is takes pilot of it, a chart of the hex (Cartography: a map carried or the draft) chart of it. reef: tile._reef; shoal: open water by a skerry (tile._skerry) or a delta's flats; bar: the mouth of a river (river or great, Rivers.band) or a delta (tile._delta / riverDistributary); fjord: tile._fjord (also slow: fjordWind). Cautious orders: hazard water costs cautiousSlow more and the ship lies to at night before an unpiloted, unlit hazard. The route planner avoids unpiloted hazards by `avoid` leagues-equivalent each, storms by stormAvoid.

pilots._doc: A local pilot hired at a port (systems/seaPassage.js hirePilot): his fee into the port's purse, by the town's size; he knows the waters within `radius` hexes of his port and takes the ship through them (risk × coast.pilot, and the planner no longer steers wide of them); aboard for the next voyage (put ashore at its end) or `days` days. Ports with a lighthouse send a pilot cutter out to a ship making for them: a harbour pilot for the last cutterReach hexes, `cutterDue` × the port's fee, taken from the purse if it holds it.

lighthouses._doc: Lighthouses at the major ports (capitals and cities on the water) and the player's own Lighthouse buildings (lighthouse_building): within `radius` hexes the night is no darker than day for the coast's dangers (coast.lit), and their ports send pilot cutters. Drawn on the world map (ui/renderer/seaWeather.js).

display._doc: The world map (ui/renderer/seaWeather.js): the wind arrow by the player's ship, storms drawn as turning cloud over charted sea, lighthouse beams after dusk.
